updates.title: H1 2026 CEO Stakeholder Update
updates.quote: We might be early, but we are not wrong
updates.summary: Our first CEO update: how Feenix moved from design and development into the market, covering training, governance, partnerships, product milestones and what comes next.

sections.heading: CEO thoughts
paragraphs: Dear all,

Welcome to the first Feenix CEO stakeholder update. Six months ago Feenix was an idea and a conviction: that the built environment is adopting AI faster than it can govern it, and that someone needed to help firms close that gap with evidence rather than opinion.

We are now operating in the market. We have partners, a platform, a training offer and a group of advisers whose job is to challenge us. Some of the conversations we are having are early. The direction is not wrong.

sections.heading: Feenix in focus
paragraphs: The first half of 2026 was the period in which Feenix moved from design and development into the market. We formally launched on 27 May 2026 with a dinner that brought together founding partners, Braintrust members and sector leaders.
Our offer now covers four connected areas: training, governance, implementation and advisory. The principle connecting all four is simple: responsible AI is a foundation, not a feature.

sections.heading: New partnerships
paragraphs: We introduced our founding partner ecosystem: Clearnorth, Serpin, Built Intelligence and Vidos. Together they cover connection to the market, governance at scale, technical grounding and day-to-day delivery.
We also began working with The QSi to support quantity surveyors with the knowledge, governance and confidence they need to adopt AI responsibly.

sections.heading: Assurance and recognition
paragraphs: Feenix was confirmed as a RICS Tech Partner and became a member of the International Association of Privacy Professionals. Both ground our work in recognised professional and regulatory standards.
In June we published The Compliance Cost Gap, a transparent model of what the RICS standard on the responsible use of AI may cost the surveying sector in its first year.

sections.heading: Product milestones
paragraphs: The FNX Governance Platform reached v1. It helps organisations move beyond a folder of AI policy documents to a connected system of policies, risks, evidence and oversight, aligned with RICS, ISO/IEC 42001 and EU AI Act principles.
Responsible with AI, our training offer, continues to develop alongside the platform so that firms can build capability and governance together.

sections.heading: Looking ahead
paragraphs: In the second half of the year we will publish practical guidance mapped to the RICS standard, launch a recurring governance intelligence series on LinkedIn, and deepen the work with our partners and early clients.
Thank you to every stakeholder, partner and adviser who has backed us this far. We will keep reporting honestly on what is working and what is not.
Micah Stennett, Founder and CEO

updates.title: The Built Environment AI Governance Intelligence Series begins
updates.summary: A recurring, source-backed briefing on how AI governance is shaping professional obligations, buyer decisions and commercial outcomes in the built environment.
body: The series runs in three layers: a Governance Pulse every 14 days, a monthly Governance Monitor, and a quarterly State of AI Governance report.
Every public conclusion traces back to a dated source, and corrections are recorded rather than quietly replaced. The first Pulse went out on 12 October 2026.

newsletters.title: The Feenix Brief, Issue 01
newsletters.hook: The question I am asked most often is: why now?
newsletters.summary: Opening note from Micah, the partner ecosystem, RICS Tech Partner and IAPP membership, the launch dinner and the Feenix Braintrust.

sections.heading: Opening note from Micah
paragraphs: The question I am asked most often is: why now?

Organisations across the built environment are moving fast because the technology is compelling. Few are moving carefully, because governance is hard. Feenix exists to make adoption defensible, not slower.
This first issue records where we are at the moment we moved into public.

sections.heading: Feenix in focus
paragraphs: Feenix introduced its founding partner ecosystem: Clearnorth (known across the sector as The QS People), Serpin, Built Intelligence and Vidos, covering the full lifecycle of responsible AI adoption.
Feenix was confirmed as a Tech Partner of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors and became a member of the International Association of Privacy Professionals.
On 27 May 2026 Feenix held its launch dinner, bringing together founding partners, Braintrust members and sector leaders.

sections.heading: What we're seeing
paragraphs: The RICS Professional Standard on the Responsible Use of AI in Surveying Practice became mandatory on 9 March 2026. Professional responsibility for advice remains with the surveyor, whether or not AI contributed to it.
Use of AI is outpacing governance. Firms that delay building governance structures face growing pressure from professional bodies, regulators and clients.

sections.heading: Looking ahead
paragraphs: Over the coming months Feenix will publish guidance, worked examples and practical tools mapped to the RICS standard.

sections.heading: The Feenix Braintrust
paragraphs: Five independent advisers whose role is to challenge us, not endorse us: Davin Dhillon (Strategy and Growth), Danielle Lodge (Enterprise Operations), Scott Druck (AI Implementation), Kate Vandermark (Communications) and Marcia Weekes-Spears (People and Organisational Change).
